## Description
Assume each tile is about 1m x 1m. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Excellent for transparent insulation, &#10;&#9;&#9;a silica aerogel tile contain nanoscale networks of interconnecting silica clusters, &#10;&#9;&#9;contain over 97% air by volume and have some of the lowest measured thermal conductivities of &#10;&#9;&#9;any known material (of 0.02 W/m/K at 1 bar pressure or 0.01 W/m/K at Martian atmospheric &#10;&#9;&#9;pressure). &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Routinely employed in many engineering applications, including &#10;&#9;&#9;NASA’s Mars Exploration Rovers where thin aerogel layers provided night-time thermal &#10;&#9;&#9;insulation. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;A 3 cm layer of silica aerogel can increase the temperature of the underlying &#10;&#9;&#9;surface by 45 K when it receives a flux of 150 W/m2. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Application : Micrometeorite / Whipple Shield Component&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;NASA studied composite aerogel multifoil (aerogel layers between metal foils) as a &#10;&#9;&#9;multi-shock Whipple shield Aerogel converts hypervelocity particle kinetic energy &#10;&#9;&#9;to thermal/mechanical energy, stopping fragments Used as the inner capture layer &#10;&#9;&#9;in a layered shield on habitat outer walls &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20130012682&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;
